entities.name: Aromatic nitro reduction
observations: The encoded transformation converts an aryl nitro group, Ar-N(=O)O, to the corresponding aryl amine, Ar-NH2; the aryl scaffold and methoxy substituents are retained.
The matched ORD evidence lists ethyl acetate as an additional component but does not expose a definitive reducing reagent, catalyst, solvent, temperature, time, or yield.

entities.name: Nitro reduction reagent classes
observations: Plausible interpretations include H2 with Pd/C, PtO2, or Raney Ni; transfer hydrogenation with ammonium formate/Pd-C; or metal-mediated reduction with Fe/NH4Cl, SnCl2/HCl, or Zn/NH4Cl.
These reagent classes are chemical interpretation rather than directly retrieved conditions for this exact record.
Ethyl acetate is compatible as a solvent or workup/extraction solvent, not as the reducing reagent or catalyst.
